correctness.rationale: Exact BH event decomposition gives FDR<=3alpha/4 under an exact uniform true-null p-value. The antithetic Gaussian model with mean -Phi^{-1}(alpha/2)-Phi^{-1}(alpha)>0 makes V<=alpha iff U>=alpha/2, obtaining equality at corr -1; almost-sure Gaussian coupling and bounded convergence give sharp supremum for -1<rho<0. For alpha=1/20, rho=-99999999/100000000, Gaussian density<1/2 and Chebyshev give P(threshold disagreement)<29/5000; hence FDR>317/10000. Equation (26) of arXiv:2212.09706v4 with e<3, pi>2 gives tilde s_2(alpha)/2<30307/1088000; exact rational cross multiplication verifies strict violation. Python exact-fraction verifier replays finite rational identities, not continuum proof.

value.rationale: A concrete positively definite bivariate Gaussian null/nonnull model violates a specifically named published conjecture about FDR under negative Gaussian dependence. The sharp supremum over every strictly negative correlation for two one-sided tests identifies why the Gaussian structural assumption cannot improve the general worst-case two-test harmonic factor. This directly informs the mathematically motivated search for dependence-aware multiple-testing corrections, not an arbitrary parameter slice or mere numerical recheck; the general arbitrary-dependence inequality itself is not claimed new.
